correctness.rationale: Write A=2^a, B=2A-1, T=σ(n)-2n=B(p+1)-p² odd. Exactly three complement orbits have odd weight: 1+Ap², (A+1)p, A+p²; all other middle/outer orbits have even weight, with even-a square-root singleton counted ONCE. Parity forces one odd orbit in any omission with at most two; 1+Ap²>T and algebra excludes both remaining singleton odds. For two orbits four cases arise (odd w2 or w3 times even middle or outer). The middle cases reduce to p dividing B or A-1 and force respectively no odd prime or the unique A=4,p=3 singleton M=2. Outer cases reduce to integer quadratics with strictly increasing positive-root branches; bounds trap a candidate between consecutive integers or force even quotient k where k must be odd. Boundary a=1,2,3 addressed explicitly. For n=36 omitted weights 13+6=19. Independent exact divisor orbit combination enumeration for a<=14, odd primes up to199 found 36 only. Finite check is not infinite proof.
